Everything you need to ship from India to Ecuador or import from Ecuador to India: the trade agreement, routes and transit times, how your buyer imports, duties, regulators and documents.
India and Ecuador at a glance
No trade agreement with India. Most Favoured Nation duties apply.
India exports pharmaceuticals, vehicles and motorcycles, steel, chemicals and textiles. India buys shrimp feed inputs, cocoa, bananas, wood and crude oil.
Routes and transit times to Ecuador
40–55 days to Guayaquil/Posorja. No direct India–West Coast services: cargo tranships in Asia (Singapore, Busan, Shanghai) and crosses the Pacific, or routes via the Panama Canal.
Transit times are indicative port-to-port from Nhava Sheva / Mundra (sea) and Delhi / Mumbai (air). Routing changes (for example Red Sea diversions) can add 10–14 days.
Importing into Ecuador: what your buyer needs
The importer registers with SENAE (Ecuapass) and needs an electronic signature token.
A customs agent is required above set value thresholds.
INEN technical regulations and certificates of conformity apply to many consumer goods.
Tariff 0–45% depending on the product, plus 15% VAT (IVA), the FODINFA levy (0.5%) and, for some goods, ICE excise.

From Ecuador to India, and tips from the field
Wood, cocoa and fruit flows. India's plant quarantine rules apply.
File the Bill of Entry through a licensed customs broker in India (YAM holds licence R-7/92).
Check the HS code in the Indian tariff, the DGFT import policy (free, restricted or prohibited) and any BIS, FSSAI, plant quarantine or other permit before the goods ship.
If an agreement applies, get the correct certificate of origin from the exporter to claim the lower duty.
Dollarised economy: no currency risk on USD invoices.
INEN conformity is the most common cause of delays.
